findings.text: [B]: stars, moon, three hills and a tiny 4 crowd the square; the 4 is the smallest element and sits at the very bottom, so the stars could go and the numeral would read.
[C]: the crescent's lower half dissolves into the light ground and survives only as a thin outline, so the dark band could go or be extended so the moon holds its shape.
[D]: one disc and one numeral, nothing to remove; the thin 4 is the weakest stroke and the dithered lower edge leaks into the white below.
[A]: a single hill and a large bold 6 — the clearest numeral of the four, but the hill alone says landscape, not painting, and the name drops the moon the others share.
All four keep the bottom third of the tile empty or light, so the icons look cut off; the frame's lower edge could go consistently or be closed.
B, C and D share one name, so the icon alone must carry the difference; the plainest one (D or C) carries it best.
